data.name: Dyana Moto
data.detailed_description:
Speed, shots and platforms. This is the frenzy of Dyana Moto. Dyana is a space biker who fights a fleet of space ships and robots on the front line in a high-level battle simulation. Your bike is a powerful tank of war, setting fire to all your enemies and jumping great distances. The attacks come from all sides and Dyana needs to stay on the platforms and always with open eyes with lots of ammunition to survive and reach the end.

Collect power ups to multiply your firepower.
Fuel your motorcycling
Practice flying jumps
Make combos (destroy enemies simultaneously, shoot back and forth) to gain thousands of points.
Open fire constantly on your enemies and destroy everything that moves on the screen.

You will save your score after destroying the final robot or choose to restart the game.

reviews.review:
Dyana Moto is a small-scale arcade action game that takes the familiar idea of motorcycle riding and pushes it into a much stranger direction. Instead of concentrating on racing lines, realistic handling, or competition against other riders, the game places its heroine on an armed futuristic motorcycle and turns each stage into a combination of shooting, jumping, survival, and score chasing. Developed by Halissoni and published by Conglomerate 5, it is clearly designed as a straightforward arcade experience where constant movement and destruction matter more than mechanical realism.

The central attraction is the unusual combination of motorcycle movement and combat. Dyana rides through environments populated by hostile robots and other threats while firing at enemies and navigating platforms. The motorcycle functions less like a conventional vehicle and more like a mobile combat machine. Large jumps allow the player to cross gaps and move between platforms, while weapons provide the means to eliminate enemies encountered along the way. This creates a gameplay rhythm in which positioning, shooting, jumping, and reacting to hazards are happening almost simultaneously.

Combat is intentionally uncomplicated. Rather than encouraging careful ammunition management or tactical encounters, Dyana Moto rewards aggressive play. Players can keep firing while moving and collect power-ups that improve offensive capability. Increasing firepower makes later encounters more manageable and contributes to the satisfying arcade sensation of becoming increasingly destructive during a successful attempt. The controls and objectives are relatively easy to understand, making the game accessible without requiring a lengthy introduction or complicated progression system.

Its scoring mechanics provide an additional reason to play aggressively. Destroying enemies efficiently and performing combos can produce substantially better scores, so simply reaching the end is not necessarily the ultimate objective. Players interested in arcade-style mastery can repeat stages or runs while attempting to improve their performance. Shooting enemies in different directions and eliminating groups within a short period can reward players who become comfortable controlling the motorcycle while maintaining awareness of everything happening around them.

The platforming component helps separate the game from an ordinary side-scrolling shooter. Jumping a motorcycle between platforms while enemies attack creates some entertaining situations, especially when a successful landing is immediately followed by another attack or obstacle. At its best, Dyana Moto creates a hectic flow where the player is jumping, firing, collecting improvements, and avoiding danger without much downtime. However, this constant activity can also become messy, and the limited mechanical complexity means repetition eventually becomes noticeable.

Presentation is modest and reflects the game's relatively small scope. The science-fiction environments, robots, spacecraft, weapons, and unusual motorcycle establish a recognizable arcade identity, but the overall visual quality is functional rather than elaborate. Players accustomed to highly polished modern action games may find the environments and effects basic. The simpler appearance is easier to appreciate when approached with expectations closer to an experimental indie arcade title than a fully developed motorcycle action franchise.

Difficulty comes primarily from managing several threats at once. Players must monitor incoming enemies while keeping the motorcycle safely positioned and preparing for jumps. Because attacks can demand attention from multiple directions, some sections become chaotic quickly. This works reasonably well for players who enjoy repeating short challenges until their reactions improve, although the difficulty does not always feel as carefully refined as it could. Occasionally, surviving the chaos feels more important than executing a deliberate strategy.

The game's limited scope is simultaneously an advantage and a weakness. There is very little unnecessary complexity, allowing players to understand what they are supposed to do almost immediately. On the other hand, there are not enough systems or variations to sustain players expecting a lengthy campaign or deep progression. Steam achievements and score improvement provide additional goals, but replay value largely depends on whether the player enjoys chasing higher scores and mastering the core mechanics.

Steam Deck compatibility should be treated as unverified rather than officially supported. The game does not have a confirmed Steam Deck compatibility rating. Its lightweight technical requirements suggest that raw performance should not be particularly demanding, but performance requirements and actual Steam Deck compatibility are different matters. Controller behavior, interface usability, Proton compatibility, and other handheld-specific considerations may therefore require manual testing or adjustments.

Ultimately, Dyana Moto succeeds more as an unusual arcade curiosity than as a fully realized action game. Riding a weaponized motorcycle while jumping between platforms and firing at robots is a distinctive premise, and the combination can produce enjoyable bursts of frantic action. Power-ups, combos, achievements, and score chasing add some replay incentive, but limited variety and relatively basic presentation prevent the experience from developing into something substantially deeper.

For players who appreciate inexpensive, obscure arcade games and enjoy improving scores through repeated attempts, there is entertainment to be found here. Those expecting realistic motorcycle mechanics, extensive levels, sophisticated combat, or polished progression will probably find the experience too limited. Its unusual concept remains its strongest quality, delivering a simple mixture of motorcycle platforming and relentless shooting that is easy to understand but comparatively quick to exhaust.

Rating: 5/10
